name: structured_resources
description: Provenance of the physiology viva-pulse wraps. viva-pulse drives the real Kitware Pulse Physiology Engine, which is Kitware's open-source continuation of the DARPA/SBIR BioGears engine — both are lumped-parameter, circuit-analog whole-body models with feedback-ODE control. The cards below describe the engines and the baroreflex control loop the hemorrhage studies rest on; each cross-links to the primary references folded into the References list.

physiology-model.name: Pulse Physiology Engine (the engine viva-pulse wraps)
physiology-model.summary: The real, open-source Kitware Pulse whole-body adult engine. Individual systems (cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, tissue, thermal, energy, environment, drug) are lumped-parameter circuit analogs coupled by differential equations for feedback, pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics and diffusion, advanced in real time. C++ with Python/Java/C#/C bindings.
physiology-model.what_viva_pulse_uses: viva-pulse wraps this engine as process-bigraph Processes (PulseProcess, PulseCircuitProcess). Every number in the studies comes from advancing this engine; there is no surrogate.
physiology-model.validation: Pulse ships a verification & validation suite covering resting physiology and 100+ disease, trauma and treatment scenarios.
physiology-model.role_in_investigation: The substrate of the whole pulse-hemorrhage investigation — the hemorrhage, resuscitation controller and all 21 patient states run on it.

physiology-model.name: BioGears (Pulse's origin engine)
physiology-model.summary: The open-source whole-body human physiology engine (originally a DARPA / TATRC program) that Kitware forked and continued as Pulse. Shares the lumped-parameter circuit-analog architecture and the PK/PD framework, and documents many of the system models and validation studies Pulse inherits.
physiology-model.relation_to_pulse: Pulse is Kitware's open-source continuation of BioGears; the cardiovascular, respiratory, renal and energy system models and their baroreflex/chemoreflex control loops trace back to the BioGears methodology.
physiology-model.role_in_investigation: Background provenance for the system models and the baroreflex the studies rely on; not run directly by viva-pulse.

physiology-model.name: Baroreflex cardiovascular control (the hemorrhage mechanism)
physiology-model.summary: The short-term arterial-pressure control loop: a fall in mean arterial pressure raises heart rate and vascular tone to defend perfusion. In the BioGears/Pulse lineage this is an explicit feedback model integrated into the whole-body cardiovascular circuit.
physiology-model.role_in_investigation: This is the emergent mechanism the hemorrhage-severity-sweep study reports (finding F-04): tachycardia defends MAP for mild bleeds and is outrun once cardiac output falls. The reference grounds that mechanism in the engine's own model rather than in outside literature.
